UNICEF Montenegro published an analysis on July 12, 2021, stating that 5G technology does not cause or spread the coronavirus. [1] The World Health Organization (WHO) also confirmed on February 27, 2020, that no adverse health effects have been causally linked with exposure to wireless technologies, including 5G. [2] The International Telecommunications Union (ITU), a UN agency, stated on April 22, 2020, that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling the theory a "hoax that has no technical basis." [3] Healthline reported on May 10, 2021, that viruses spread through respiratory droplets, not wireless networks, and there is no proof that 5G affects the risk of developing viral infections. [4] Full Fact, an independent fact-checking charity, explored these claims and found no evidence to suggest a link between 5G and COVID-19, noting that the virus was spreading in areas without 5G networks. [5] The claim that 5G causes or spreads coronavirus has been widely debunked by scientific evidence and health organizations. [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]
